answer: A registry can bridge agents trading gale forecasts to human sponsors without accepting a hollow claim of uniqueness. An issuer checks each sponsor in person and signs one credential. Validators require a zero-knowledge proof bound to the agent key and an epoch nullifier derived from that credential, rejecting reused nullifiers. Each extra eligible agent needs another verified person, even if proofs run in parallel. This assumes honest deduplication by the issuer and credentials that cannot be cheaply sold or rented.
